claim: Quillstack retries failed webhook deliveries for up to three days.

passages.text: Quillstack webhooks: configure an endpoint URL and choose which events to subscribe to from the dashboard.
If your endpoint does not answer with a 2xx status, we keep resending the event on an exponential schedule for 72 hours before giving up and marking it as dead.
Each delivery is signed with an HMAC-SHA256 header so you can verify that the payload came from us.
Webhook payloads are limited to 256 KB; larger objects are sent as a reference you can fetch from the API.

claim: The Larkspur Maps geocoding API allows 600 requests per minute on the Business plan.

passages.text: Rate limits by plan — Free: 60 requests per minute. Business: 600 requests per minute, bursts up to 1,200. Enterprise: custom limits negotiated with sales.
Larkspur Maps also offers a static tiles endpoint that is cached at the edge and does not count toward your rate limit.

passages.source: Larkspur Maps community forum: 429 errors when backfilling
passages.text: Forum: we hit 429s on the Free plan almost immediately when backfilling 50k addresses, upgrading fixed it.
The routing API has a separate limit of 100 requests per minute on all paid plans.

claim: Ferrow DB has a native JSON column type as of version 4.

passages.text: (Blog, May 2023) Ferrow DB 3.2 has no native JSON type, so most teams store documents in TEXT columns and parse them in the application.
Ferrow DB 4.0 release notes (February 2025): introduces a native JSON column type with path indexes and the ->> operator.
Ferrow DB is an embedded SQL database written in Rust, designed for edge deployments.
Upgrading from 3.x to 4.0 requires a one-time migration of the on-disk format; see ferrow migrate --help.

claim: Brindle CLI runs on Windows.

passages.text: Install Brindle with Homebrew: brew install brindle/tap/brindle.
Prebuilt binaries are published for macOS, Linux, and Windows, each for x64 and arm64, on every tagged release.
Brindle reads its configuration from brindle.toml in the project root, or from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brindle.

claim: Ostrava Queue guarantees message ordering within a partition.

passages.text: Ostrava Queue docs, Delivery semantics: messages within a single partition are always delivered to consumers in the order they were produced. There is no ordering guarantee across partitions.

passages.source: Ostrava Queue community forum: message ordering question
passages.text: Forum reply: I think ordering isn't really guaranteed, we saw some messages arrive out of order last week, but we might have had multiple partitions configured.
Ostrava Queue supports at-least-once delivery; consumers should be idempotent.
Partitions can be added to a topic at any time, but never removed.
Pricing is based on throughput units, each allowing 1 MB/s of ingress.

claim: Pylon UI 2.0 was released in March 2026.

passages.text: December 2025: the Pylon UI team announced the 2.0 beta, with a new theming engine and smaller bundle size.
Releases · pylon-ui/pylon: v2.0.0 — released 2026-03-11. Stable release of the 2.0 line. See the migration guide for breaking changes.
v1.9.4 — released 2026-01-20. Security fix for the tooltip component.
Pylon UI is a component library for React and Solid.

claim: Tessel Cloud's Starter plan costs $9 per month when billed monthly.

passages.text: Starter — $9/mo billed monthly, or $90/year billed annually. Includes 3 projects and 100 GB bandwidth.
Team — $29 per seat per month, with SSO and audit logs.
All plans include a 14-day free trial; no credit card is required to start.
Reddit: Tessel used to be $7 for Starter back in 2023, they bumped it at some point.

claim: Harbor RPC does not require TLS for connections on localhost.

passages.text: Security: TLS is mandatory for all remote connections. Loopback connections (127.0.0.1 and ::1) may use plaintext to simplify local development.
Harbor RPC generates client stubs for Go, TypeScript and Kotlin from .harbor schema files.
Mutual TLS can be enabled per service with the requireClientCert option.

claim: Quillstack's REST API supports batch deletes.

passages.text: Quillstack REST API reference — Records: list, create, update, delete.
The REST API does not support batch deletion. Delete records one at a time, or use the bulk import/export tool to replace a whole table.
Batch creates are supported: POST up to 100 records in one request to /v2/records:batchCreate.
Rate limit: 10 requests per second per API key.

claim: A single PUT request to Marlow Storage can upload an object of up to 1 TB.

passages.text: Upload limits: a single PUT request can upload an object of at most 100 GB. Use multipart upload for objects up to 5 TB.
Marlow Storage is S3-compatible, so most existing S3 SDKs work by changing the endpoint URL.
Each multipart part must be between 5 MB and 5 GB, except the last part.
Egress to the internet is billed at $0.01 per GB after the first 1 TB each month.

claim: Ferrow Cloud's free tier includes 10 GB of storage.

passages.text: (Pricing page snapshot, 2024) Free tier: 10 GB storage, 1 database, community support.
Pricing update, effective January 1, 2026: the free tier now includes 2 GB of storage per account, down from 10 GB. Existing free accounts keep 10 GB until July 2026.
Ferrow Cloud is the managed hosting service for Ferrow DB.
Paid plans start at $15/month with 50 GB storage.

claim: The Larkspur Maps routing API is free for the first 100,000 calls each month.

passages.text: Geocoding includes 100,000 free calls per month on every plan; after that, $0.40 per 1,000 calls.
Routing calls are billed from the first request at $0.50 per 1,000 calls. There is no free monthly allotment for routing.
Larkspur Maps routing supports driving, cycling and walking profiles.
Usage resets on the first day of each calendar month (UTC).

claim: Kestrel.js 5 dropped support for Node.js 18.

passages.text: Kestrel.js 5.0 is a major release focused on the new router and streaming responses.
Supported runtimes: Kestrel.js 5 still supports Node.js 18, 20 and 22. Node.js 18 support will be removed in Kestrel.js 6.
Kestrel.js 4 reached end of life on 2026-06-30.
Bun and Deno are supported experimentally.

claim: Brindle Labs is headquartered in Berlin.

passages.text: About us: Brindle Labs is headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, with a sales office in Berlin and a remote engineering team across Europe.
Brindle Labs opened its Berlin office in 2025 to serve customers in the DACH region.
The company raised a $12M Series A in 2024.

claim: Tessel Cloud functions automatically run in the region closest to each user.

passages.text: Tessel Cloud has data centers in 9 regions across North America, Europe and Asia.
Functions run in the single region you choose at deploy time (default us-east-1). They are not moved closer to users automatically; put a CDN in front for static assets.
Static sites on Tessel are served from the edge in every region.
Cold starts for functions average under 200 ms.

claim: Harbor RPC uses UDP as its transport.

passages.text: Harbor RPC runs over HTTP/2 on TCP. There is no UDP transport.
Harbor RPC's streaming calls are multiplexed over a single connection.
Our metrics agent sends UDP packets to the collector, separate from Harbor RPC traffic.
Message encoding uses a compact binary format similar to Protocol Buffers.

claim: Pylon UI 1.x supports server-side rendering.

passages.text: Pylon UI 2 supports server-side rendering through the renderToStream helper.
The 1.x line receives security fixes until the end of 2026.
Pylon UI components are written in TypeScript and ship type definitions.
Theming in 2.0 uses CSS variables instead of the 1.x runtime theme provider.

claim: Object lock is available in every Marlow Storage region.

passages.text: Object lock is available in us-east, eu-west and ap-south.
Object lock prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a retention period you set.
Versioning must be enabled on a bucket before object lock can be turned on.

claim: Ostrava Queue charges extra for keeping messages longer than 7 days.

passages.text: Ostrava Queue keeps messages for 7 days by default. Retention can be raised to 30 days per topic.
Messages longer than 1 MB are rejected; store large payloads elsewhere and send a reference.
Throughput units are billed per hour.
Consumers can replay messages from any offset still in retention.

claim: Northwind Cloud is acquiring the company behind Kestrel.js.

passages.text: Hacker News comment: reportedly Northwind has been in talks with the Kestrel maintainers for months, but nothing has been confirmed by either side.
Kestrel.js is maintained by Kestrel Software GmbH and community contributors.
Northwind Cloud announced a $2M sponsorship of open-source web frameworks in 2026.
Kestrel.js has over 40,000 stars on GitHub.

claim: Quillstack Forms accepts file uploads up to 50 MB.

passages.text: Quillstack Docs attachments can be up to 50 MB each.
Quillstack Forms can send each new response to Slack or email.
Quillstack Forms responses are stored for 2 years on the Business plan.
Upload large files to Quillstack Drive and share a link.

claim: Ferrow DB replication is synchronous by default.

passages.text: Ferrow DB supports both synchronous and asynchronous replication.
Synchronous replication waits for at least one replica to confirm each write.
Replicas can be read from, but writes always go to the primary.
Ferrow DB 4.1 added automatic failover.

claim: Tessel Cloud had a multi-region outage in August 2026.

passages.text: Status history — July 14, 2026: elevated error rates for functions in eu-west for 40 minutes. Resolved.
August 19, 2026: scheduled database maintenance in us-east-1, 02:00–03:00 UTC. Completed as planned.
Tessel Cloud publishes incident postmortems within 5 business days.
Multi-region deployments are available on the Team plan and above.

claim: The Larkspur Maps iOS SDK supports offline map tiles.

passages.text: The Android SDK supports offline map tiles that you download per region.
The iOS SDK supports SwiftUI and UIKit, and requires iOS 16 or later.

passages.source: Larkspur Maps — Offline maps and quotas
passages.text: Offline maps count toward your monthly tile quota when they are downloaded.
Both mobile SDKs are open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

claim: Velloro 1.x supports hot module reload.

passages.text: Install with npm install velloro, then run velloro dev to start the development server.
Hot module reload works out of the box, with no configuration needed.
This release rewrites the bundler in Rust for faster builds.

claim: Saltmarsh ORM 3 can generate migrations automatically.

passages.text: Queries are built with a chainable builder and run with .execute().
This version requires Node.js 22 or later.
Generates migration files automatically by comparing your schema with the database.
Saltmarsh is an open-source ORM for TypeScript.

claim: The Ivydale Basic plan includes audit logs.

passages.text: Basic, Team and Enterprise plans can be billed monthly or yearly.
Includes audit logs kept for one year, plus SAML single sign-on.
Up to 5 users and 20 GB of storage.

claim: Coppice CRM Community Edition supports custom fields.

passages.source: Coppice CRM Cloud Edition — Admin guide
passages.text: Custom fields can be added to any record type from the admin settings.
Self-host it with Docker Compose on any Linux server.
We ship a new release every six weeks.

claim: Sundial Agent supports ARM64 Linux.

passages.text: Sundial Agent collects host metrics and forwards them to Sundial Console.
Runs on x64 and ARM64 Linux, as well as macOS.
Billing is per monitored host, per month.

claim: Tarnby Mail supports end-to-end encryption.

passages.text: Import your existing mailbox over IMAP in a few minutes.
Tarnby builds privacy-focused productivity apps.
Everything you store is end-to-end encrypted, and the keys never leave your devices.
All systems operational.

claim: Glasswing 3.0 supports WebSocket connections.

passages.text: Routes are declared in a routes.yaml file.
Supports WebSocket connections alongside regular HTTP routes.
Has anyone benchmarked it against other web servers?

claim: Ruddock Search's Pro plan includes 50,000 queries per month.

passages.text: Includes 1,000 queries per month.
Send queries with GET /v1/search?q=<terms>.
Includes 50,000 queries per month and email support.
We added result highlighting to every plan.
